content.comment_body: I am using [product_name] V5.0 on a Linux workstation (Ubuntu 8.04) and need to upgrade to [product_name] V6, since the [product_name] [article_no] modules are soon unavailable. I also have a Windows XP laptop for fieldwork, which I have upgraded to V6 successfully. First, is there a free upgrade path from V5 to V6 for Linux, or do I need to purchase a full V6 license? On Windows, I had to upgrade first to V5.0.23, then to V6. The online update tool in [product_name] for Linux seems similar: after downloading and applying the update, the script finishes without error, but the software fails to start with a 'java.lang.UnsupportedClassVersionError' message. The upgrade process seems to mainly replace the file Tools/Application/lib/classes.jar. Reverting this file restores previous (un-upgraded) functionality. Has anyone managed to make this upgrade work on Linux? Any advice on what I might be missing? There were also issues installing from the original [product_name] V5.0 CD; the installation procedure links incorrectly to the Linux directory. Bypassing this (by manually launching 'sh Linx/Setup.bin') leads to a permission error on JRE. Eventually, I copied the CD's Linux directory to the hard drive and gave full permissions, then starting the shell script 'Tools/Application/[product_name]' allowed me to run the application OK and work with projects. So my third question is: could the way I installed affect the upgrade process, and is there a better procedure available? Best regards, [user_name]
A new question posted by [user_name] has been moved to a separate thread titled 'execute the command for [product_name] installation'. Best regards [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: A user encounters challenges upgrading [product_name] from V5.0 to V6 on Linux, facing unclear upgrade options, Java compatibility errors after updating, and installation difficulties with the original CD. The central issues concern compatibility, transparency in the upgrade process, and installation reliability, impacting both user experience and perceived Linux support.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects a transparent and reliable upgrade path from V5.0 to V6 on Linux, similar to the Windows experience, as well as a seamless installation process that does not require manual workarounds.
